problem:
From **top to bottom,** the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola $(y-1)^{2}-4(x+1)^{2}=5$ are

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $)\,$
and
$\,($
{{field-3}}, 
{{field-4}} $).$
worked_solution:
To find the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-1)^{2}-4(x+1)^{2} & =5 \\ (y-1)^{2}-4(0+1)^{2} & =5 \\ (y-1)^{2}-4 & =5 \\ (y-1)^{2} & =9 \\ y-1 & =\pm 3 \\ y & =1\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

So, from top to bottom, the $y$-intercepts are $(0,4)$ and $(0,-2).$
